title: Introduce SLO Pacing Controller and Egress Bottleneck Mitigator
text:
Introduce SLO Pacing Controller and Egress Bottleneck Mitigator

description:
Motivation: During a recent incident we observed rapid accept/reject oscillation on tenant routes when node-level egress became constrained and SLO budgets dropped. This PR introduces a SLO Pacing Controller that applies a short-term, smoothly decaying acceptance window per-tenant to avoid rapid reopen cycles, plus an Egress Bottleneck Mitigator that tracks cluster egress credit pressure and proactively throttles egress-heavy request classes (model downloads, large-embedding exports, cross-region replication) so serving paths stay within SLOs. The two mechanisms are designed to operate together: pacing reduces traffic spikes at the request ingress while the egress mitigator prevents downstream piping from amplifying pressure. Key changes: 1) runtime/pacing: add slo_pacer module with adaptive window sizing, exponential decay on allowance, and metrics hooks (slo.pacer.pressure, slo.pacer.window_ms). 2) routing/egress: egress_credit_manager that aggregates per-zone egress usage and exposes per-route admission signals; a soft-deny path for high-cost egress requests with a tokenized retry hint. 3) telemetry: new Prometheus gauges and logs with structured reason codes to aid post-incident analysis. 4) safety hotfix: reconcile circuit-breaker reopen debounce to avoid double-reopening when pacing and CB both release simultaneously. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is opt-in via config flags (runtime.slo_pacer.enabled, routing.egress_mitigator.enabled) and safe defaults preserve existing flow when disabled. Migration: no DB schema changes. Feature gate and rollout: added rollout flag to Console (console rollout metadata included in docs). Checklist: - [x] design doc reviewed (ENG-2048) - [x] unit tests for slo_pacer core logic - [x] integration tests against mocked egress manager - [x] load test scenario showing reduction in reopen oscillations - [x] telemetry dashboards prototypes - [x] docs + console flag UI patch - [x] incident runbook entry updated Testing notes: local unit/integration, k8s staging soak (24h) with synthetic spike pattern, and canary on two low-traffic regions. Observed 45% reduction in rapid reopens and 30% lower cross-region egress bursts in staging. Known limitations: pacing currently operates on request-count windows, future work will add token-bucket per-tenant sizing using historical latency profiles. Related work: follows up on ENG-2101 (connection stabilization) and complements existing circuit logic from ENG-1783. Merge: squash-merged after addressing reviewer feedback and a single CI rerun for flaky e2e coverage.

review_comments:
Diego Alvarez: Nice direction. Please add a unit test that covers the exponential decay path when allowance is zero to prevent silent re-open loops.
Maya Chen: Added test covering decay and edge-case where tenant allowance flips from 0 to >0 within the same epoch; also added comment linking to ENG-2048 design notes.
Noah Patel: Telemetry looks good. Can you include a histogram for time-in-pacer-window so we can profile hotspots?
Maya Chen: Added slo.pacer.window_ms histogram and dashboard JSON in docs. Adjusted labels to include tenant_id for aggregation.
Priya Singh: e2e flakiness observed on arm64 runner. Please rerun e2e and confirm no perf regression on A100/GPU nodes.
Maya Chen: Reran e2e after narrowing the mocked egress burst timings; CI flake was unrelated (timeout on infra); rerun succeeded and I pushed a small sleep/timing tolerance in test harness.
